title: Two-passage pacing
summary: Allocate time across two comprehension passages, park uncertain items and use a protected checking buffer without sacrificing textual evidence.

sections.title: Protect the second passage and the final check
content: Strong comprehension under time pressure still uses the E5 routines: map the passage, track references, infer word meaning, retrieve stated evidence, bound inferences, and identify purpose, tone and main idea.
The pacing risk is uneven attention. One difficult item in Passage A can consume the time needed for Passage B and remove the chance to check either text.

sections.title: Use Survey, Solve, Park and Return
content: Survey: inspect both titles, text types, lengths and question stems before solving. This is a route plan, not a full first reading.

Solve: read one passage and answer questions whose evidence you can locate and justify. Park: mark an uncertain item after one focused attempt and continue. Return: use the protected buffer to revisit marked items and verify answer transfer.

For this rehearsal, use an eighteen-minute target: one minute to survey, seven minutes for each passage and three minutes to return and check. Treat it as a training target to adjust from evidence, not as an official exam allocation.

sections.title: Choose an order deliberately
content: Starting with the shorter or more familiar text can build momentum, while starting with the denser text can protect it from end-of-task fatigue. Either order is valid when you decide before reading and reserve equal attention for the other passage.

Do not switch passages repeatedly. Complete one text's first pass, park its unresolved items, then move to the second. Repeated switching adds rereading cost and makes reference chains harder to hold.

sections.title: Mark uncertainty with a reason
content: Use one brief code beside a parked item: L for location not found, M for meaning unclear, I for inference too broad, or C for two close choices. A reason tells you what to inspect when you return.
Before leaving an item, eliminate options contradicted by the passage. When you return, compare only the remaining choices against the exact sentence, paragraph purpose or whole-passage message.

sections.title: Run the eighteen-minute rehearsal
content: Survey the harbour sound-map report and the reflective ferry-bell passage. Choose an order and record your start time for each text. Complete four questions per passage.
At minute fifteen, stop first-pass solving even if an item remains uncertain. Use the final three minutes for parked questions, missing responses and a quick evidence check.

sections.title: Audit the reading and the clock
content: Single-item stall: I spent more than one focused attempt without parking the question. Passage imbalance: I left too little time for the second text. Unsupported speed: I chose an answer without locating evidence. Buffer loss: I used the final minutes for new reading instead of returns and checks.
After submission, record which error occurred and one concrete adjustment. Pacing improves when later targets respond to your actual completion and accuracy pattern.

sections.title: Harbour voices
content: Complete two original passages and eight questions using the eighteen-minute rehearsal target. Submit after the return-and-check buffer; feedback appears for the complete group.
